extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and policymakers (labor and war agencies)
extracted.subtask_description: Recommendations and standards reported for reducing absenteeism in wartime industry (plant-level and community measures), plus related administrative standards (War Labor Board review limits on arbitration awards and directives on propaganda coordination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent industrial accidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevent industrial accidents, which cause a great many absences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as the first corrective/ preventive measure to reduce absenteeism at wartime plants; presented as an item in a multi-point plan aimed at attacking absenteeism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct working conditions causing minor illness and fatigue
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct the working conditions which cause minor illness and excessive fatigue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a plant-level corrective measure to reduce absences by addressing root workplace causes of minor illness and exhaustion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide medical and health supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of good medical or health supervision to cure, prevent and shorten illness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medical/health services at the plant recommended to reduce downtime from illness and speed return-to-work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local solution of transportation problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Local solution of transportation problems by company and community cooperation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transportation problems are estimated to cause about thirty per cent of the absences; community/company cooperation recommended to address this major cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure community cooperation on household problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Secure community cooperation on household problems; marketing, laundry, etc., shopping hours, child-care problems, medical and dental services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addressing non-work household/community causes of absence through local services and cooperative arrangements is recommended as part of an attendance-improvement program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let every plant keep absence records with alleged cause
rubrics_metrics.description: Let every plant keep records of absences with the alleged cause in every case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keeping case-by-case records is recommended to isolate trends, identify causes and manage follow-up on absences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define 'absence' consistently across departments
rubrics_metrics.description: Define absence in the same terms in each department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniform definitions reduce ambiguity and ensure consistent handling and measurement of absenteeism across a plant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop systematic rules for permitted and excusable absence
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop systematic [rules] about permitted and excusable absence—such as jury duty, voting, death and illness in the family, personal illness, doctor and dentist attendance, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish explicit categories of excused absence so personnel and management have clear expectations and consistent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide permissions system and personnel follow-up for absences
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a system of permissions for certain classes of absence planned in advance through the personnel office; provide for a personnel officer to follow up on all unexcused absences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative controls (permission processes) and active follow-up on unexcused absences are recommended for management of attendance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure cooperation of labor and employers for discipline and solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Secure the cooperation of labor and employers in particular plants to (a) overcome [causes of absence] and (b) to discipline [where necessary].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint labor-management cooperation is framed as essential both to remove causes of absenteeism and to apply discipline fairly when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and praise steady attendance and effective work
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize, praise and comment the steady attendance and effective work and effort of the vast majority of American workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive reinforcement and public recognition of good attendance is recommended as part of an overall strategy to reduce absenteeism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolate and identify occasional shirkers
rubrics_metrics.description: By this method isolate and identify the occasional shirker who is absent for frivolous or no reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using recordkeeping, definitions and follow-up to single out and address individuals whose absences are non-legitimate is advised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discourage absenteeism without firing
rubrics_metrics.description: Discourage absenteeism without having to discharge men as a disciplinary measure in a time of labor shortage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy preference is expressed for disciplinary alternatives to firing during labor shortages — e.g., fines, follow-up, and administrative sanctions rather than permanent dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use fines for deliberate and repetitive shirkers
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggests fines: 'deliberate and repetitive shirkers could be fined for absences.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fines are proposed as a disciplinary tool for repeat offenders; the discussion also notes that for eligible males draft boards might be involved in sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: WLB review limited to compatibility with wage stabilization program
rubrics_metrics.description: War Labor Board will review wage awards of arbitrators only on the question of whether the award is compatible with the national wage stabilization program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal policy: the Board will not review other issues in arbitrators' awards; this limitation is justified to preserve parties' rights to arbitration and to strengthen, not weaken, voluntary arbitration. Vice-Chairman Geor[ge] Taylor's opinion emphasizes prompt and expeditious settlement methods and limiting review to stabilization-compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate propaganda with military plans and chiefs of staff approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Program in areas of 'actual or projected military operations' shall be co-ordinated with military plans through the proper agencies of the Army and Navy and would be subject to approval of the chiefs of staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: White House order assigning the propaganda field to the Office of War Information (OWI) specified this coordination and approval requirement; OWI authority was also limited so it 'shall not extend to the western hemisphere... except within the United States and Canada.'
